escena: Same woman, same grandmother, same store and same framing as the reference photo, only the mood and the work have changed: the assistant is now smiling, relaxed, scanning a small paper gift slip with a handheld barcode scanner held firmly in one complete well-formed hand, her other hand flat on a clean, tidy white counter — the box of loose paper receipts and the handwritten tags are gone; beside her a tablet shows an abstract product card with a horizontal strip of colored size blocks where exactly one block is highlighted in green, and a small profile card with a colored age dot, no words on the screen; the same grandmother stands across the counter receiving the same small red child's dress in a larger size, her hand complete with five well-formed fingers taking the hanger, the racks behind now neatly arranged: tiny two-piece outfits on small child hangers sorted by age with plain colored disc dividers, a low table of folded full-length baby rompers and packaged onesies, the flat fluorescent light replaced by soft warm LED light. No extra people, no little girl, no other employee, only the same two women. CHILDREN RULE (must be obeyed literally): every child in frame is fully dressed — babies wear a full-length long romper with socks, never just a diaper cover, never barefoot, never bare-legged — every child is accompanied by an adult, every child is on the sales floor or at the counter, and no child is inside, next to, or anywhere near a fitting room; no fitting rooms or curtains visible. HANDS AND BODIES: every hand is complete and anatomically correct with five separate well-formed fingers and visible nails, no fused, melted, mitten-like or malformed hands; every arm is clearly attached to its own person and clearly separated from other people's arms, no floating or orphan hands, feet or limbs, no extra limbs; it is visually obvious who is holding each object. NO TEXT: no readable text, letters or numbers anywhere in the image — not on garments, not on boxes, labels, tags or dividers, not on screens, not on signage or price tags; no logos, no brands, no licensed cartoon characters; garment prints are plain colors, simple stripes, small stars or a cleanly drawn little animal, never a melted or garbled graphic; any software screen shows abstract UI only — a strip of colored size blocks, a profile card with a colored age dot, garment thumbnails, soft gray placeholder lines, color chips — never words and never black censor bars. MEXICAN CHILDRENSWEAR IDENTITY: unmistakably a Mexican children's and baby clothing store — low racks at child height, tiny two-piece outfits on small child-size hangers, size dividers by age (color discs only), a baby section with folded full-length rompers and packaged onesies, a gift-wrapping table with pastel tissue paper and ribbon, everything at child scale, no adult-size garments anywhere, a street-front or Mexican shopping-plaza store with warm light and Mexican people. Editorial photo, warm natural light, real people working, photorealistic, shallow depth of field, not a 3D render, not an illustration.
